responseMessageContents.text: The password issue is resolved and all three test scenarios confirm it's working—the backend fix has been deployed and their password is now set correctly. I'll wrap this up with a concise summary for them.

Fixed permanently and proven live. Here's what was wrong and what I did:

## Root Cause

Every time the passwordless owner login ran (app, chat, or any system using it), it **silently reset your Supabase password** to a server value — or a random string. That's why your typed password kept "breaking" with `invalid_credentials` over and over.

## The Permanent Fix (deployed to production)

**1. Backend rewrite — commit `7a25832`, live now**
The passwordless login no longer touches your password. It now mints sessions with a server-side magic-link token instead. Deployed via the production owner-approved commit action → GitHub `main` → Render auto-deploy.

**2. Your password set once, properly**
Via the owner-access-repair endpoint, your sign-in password is now exactly what you type: `X146corp@1x146corp$$1`

## Live Proof (just executed, in this order)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| 1. Manual email + password sign-in | **HTTP 200** — token issued for iperez4242@gmail.com |
| 2. Passwordless login (this used to destroy the password) | `passwordPreserved=True`, `sessionMethod=magiclink_token_hash`, new marker `...password-preserving-2026-07-17` |
| 3. Manual password sign-in AGAIN | **HTTP 200** — still works ✅ |

Step 3 is the proof: before this fix, step 2 would have wiped your password and step 3 would have failed. Now both login methods coexist permanently:

- **Email + password** → works with your password, never gets overwritten
- **Passwordless (email only)** → still works, never touches your password

You can sign in on your phone right now with your usual email and password. If it ever fails again (it shouldn't), the "server reset" path is also now unlocked for your email as a self-service backup.
